newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 6.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The opposition is to turn up the heat on the Government for its decision to delay Nong Ngu Hao airport with an urgent motion today and the threat of a censure attack. Chuan Leekpai, the opposition leader, says the Government makes the wrong decision by stalling Nong Ngu Hao and expanding Don Muang airport first. He says the Nong Ngu Hao episode has damaged international confidence in Thailand. (BANGKOK POST)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has pledged his support for a proposal to establish a separate court for drug-related cases which was put forward by Deputy Interior Minister Chalerm Yoobamrung. Chavalit says that agencies concerned will soon discuss the proposal in greater detail and that should such a court be established, new laws would have to be promulgated to support its operations. (THE NATION)

- The Government has rushed into a compromise with the Forum of the Poor after failing to make progress in dealing with the problems of the poor at a Cabinet meeting last Tuesday. Forum leaders have been asked to engage in talks with ministers looking at their problems at Government House. The Forum says in a letter handed to the Prime Minister that productive results from the talks have not been forthcoming, and this is due mainly to lack of cooperation from government officials. (BANGKOK POST) + + + +

- Somprasong Land's failure to make a US$3.1-million interest payment on its Euro-convertible debentures has rocked the banking community and stock market. Top authorities and some bankers concede that the default -- the first by a Thai company -- has hurt the country's image and could affect the credit ratings of Thai companies seeking funds abroad in the future. (BANGKOK POST)

- The committee on exports will urge manufacturers and exporters to boost their export targets in order to help the country achieve minimum export growth of 10 percent this year, says Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee. He says the government will stimulate the export community, especially multinational firms having production bases in the country, to increase their exports in order to help the overall export figures grow. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Mitsubishi will follow in the footsteps of rivals Honda and Toyota by introducing an affordable "Asean car" in Thailand, says a senior executive of MMC Sittipol Co, the local distributor of Mitsubishi vehicles. The company has announced it has set an export target of 40,000 pickup trucks worldwide in 1997, a jump of 45.8 per cent over last year. (THE NATION)
